title: Opioid Days Supply and the Quantity Limit Renewal Ceiling
content:
Concurrent opioid use changes how the renewal approval ceiling of a quantity limit renewal on an acute migraine drug is worked out under the Utilization Management Program, starting from the drug's limit times the multiple applied to it.

| Member's paid oxycodone-acetaminophen retail fills dated within the last three months | Treatment of the limit times the multiple |
|---|---|
| add up to 30 or more days supply | one unit for each average monthly opioid day (those days supply divided by 3) is subtracted, a day of opioid treatment displacing one acute migraine dose |
| add up to between 1 and 29 days supply | multiplied by 0.9 |
| no such fill | used as it stands |

The fills are paid retail claims under the Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit. The three months end on the decision date: a fill counts when dated after the same day of the month three months before the decision date. The days supply of all such fills is added together before the comparison. The figure is carried forward unrounded; the renewal approval ceiling is rounded down to a whole unit only at the end.

## Worked figures (hypothetical: limit times the multiple is 13.5)

- 0 opioid days: 13.5.
- 15 opioid days: 13.5 multiplied by 0.9 gives 12.15.
- 30 opioid days: 30 divided by 3 is 10; 13.5 less 10 gives 3.5.
- 33 opioid days: 33 divided by 3 is 11; 13.5 less 11 gives 2.5.
